title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Managing the Process - Pre-Bid Meetings
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency is hosting a highly complex IT infrastructure procurement. The buyer decides to hold a Pre-Proposal Conference and designates it as 'Mandatory.' What is the direct consequence for a vendor who fails to attend?
options: Their proposal will be evaluated with a 10% penalty
They are prohibited from submitting a proposal, and any submission they make will be rejected as non-responsive
They must write an apology letter to the procurement director
They can substitute attendance by sending an email the following day
questions.explain: When a pre-bid or pre-proposal conference is explicitly designated as 'Mandatory,' attendance is a prerequisite for bidding. Any bids from absent vendors must be automatically rejected to ensure fairness.

questions.q: During an optional pre-bid conference, a vendor asks a highly technical question about the specifications. The project manager gives a verbal answer that slightly changes the published specification. As the buyer, how must you handle this?
options: Do nothing, since all attendees heard the answer verbally
Inform the group that verbal statements are not binding, and a formal written addendum must be issued to officially change the specification
Ask the vendor to write the addendum for the agency
Cancel the bid completely because specifications cannot be altered
questions.explain: A foundational rule of public procurement is that verbal instructions or answers provided during a pre-bid conference do not alter the bid document. Changes are only official when issued in a formal written addendum.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Why might a buyer choose to make a site visit 'Optional' rather than 'Mandatory' for a standard commercial service like window washing?
options: To reduce the risk of accidentally exposing the vendors to each other
To minimize restrictive barriers to entry, thereby maximizing the number of competitors
To guarantee that out-of-state vendors will win the award
questions.explain: Mandatory meetings restrict competition by automatically eliminating anyone who cannot attend. Making visits optional ensures more vendors can bid, which is appropriate for routine, straightforward tasks where seeing the site isn't strictly necessary for a valid bid.
